sections.h2: Which way should I sell a Gastonia house?
sections.html:
A Gastonia homeowner has three realistic moves: engage a realtor, find a purchaser without help, or accept cash for the place as it stands. How much work the house needs, how soon you must close and how big a discount you will tolerate for speed settle it.

  • Realtor: the broadest audience, paid for with staging effort, open times and a commission.
  • Unaided: you keep the commission and write every contract term.
  • Cash: you choose the date and skip the punch list, normally for less money.

A lot of local housing stock is from the mill years, which is why cash offers come up so often for homes with put-off maintenance.

The city started as a railroad depot in 1873, incorporated in 1877 and expanded around its textile mills. With more than 72,000 residents on about 51.99 square miles, it leads Gaston County's 15 municipalities.

Houses go back a long way here, and the ones put up during the textile boom often have aging electrical, pipes and footings. Price an inspection into your thinking before you name an asking figure.

sections.h2: How Gaston County values a Gastonia house
sections.html:
Every parcel is valued by the Gaston County tax office. In 2025 the commissioners voted for a four-year cycle of reappraisals, double the pace the eight-year state ceiling demands. Phone the tax office to learn your assessed value today and when the next reappraisal lands.

To compute a bill, divide the tax value by 100 and multiply by the rate. Budget season brings a published revenue-neutral rate from the county and each city, so a bigger value does not always mean a bigger bill.

Gaston County bills are due each September 1, and G.S. 105-360 starts interest on January 6.

Selling with a bill unpaid? Tell the closing attorney, who can settle it out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: Where a Gastonia sale is recorded
sections.html:
The Gaston County register of deeds receives the deed. Your closing attorney usually files it and lists the fees on your settlement statement, which you should request in writing ahead of closing.

Gastonia became the county seat after a 1906 referendum moved it from Dallas, so the register of deeds, the clerk's office and the tax office all serve local owners. The courthouse is at North Marietta Street and Long Avenue. Estate matters tied to a sale are filed there, and your attorney can do that for you.

sections.h2: Tax relief at 65 or with a disability
sections.html:
North Carolina has three relief programs and lets you use one, applied for on Form AV-9 at the county assessor's office. The elderly or disabled exclusion takes off the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value, with a 2026 income limit of $38,800 printed on the state form.

The disabled veteran exclusion is its own program. The assessor can tell you which fits and what deadline your parcel faces.

Small estates may skip full administration through an affidavit, and G.S. 28A-25-1 sets a $20,000 personal property limit for an intestate estate. Real estate is different, so an estate attorney or the court clerk should tell you who may sign the deed before any offer is accepted.

When back tax is also owed, gather the clerk's file, the balance due and the chain of deeds at once. A missing page in any of the three is the usual reason an inherited closing stalls.

Before anyone tours the house, settle three questions: how old are the big systems, what paperwork covers the lot, and who is allowed to sign. Older mill-era homes are often solid yet hide dated electrical, plumbing and footings, and an early inspection shows what a buyer's inspector will report.

  • Book an inspector, or a roofer and an electrician, to put numbers on the large items.
  • Read your Gaston County parcel record for wrong square footage or bedroom counts.
  • Locate the deed, a survey and a payoff letter for every loan or lien.
  • With an inherited house, ask the clerk or an attorney who holds signing power.

Appraisers compare similar sales, so unrecorded improvements can make a house look cheaper than it is, and data errors can make it look pricier. Take any mistake to the tax office before it shows up on a bill.

Lock up an empty house and mow it, because neglected lots draw complaints. Cash buyers will often take such a house unrepaired, so owners of a vacant mill-district house often weigh that against repairing and listing.

sections.h2: How long a Gastonia sale takes
sections.html:
Ask each buyer for a closing date in writing, since the route drives the calendar. A listing runs through showings, an offer, an inspection period and the buyer's loan, and a repair request can restart talks. Cash deals can close sooner since nobody is waiting on a lender's appraisal.

Your attorney handles the search for liens, the closing and the recording, and can tell you how soon the deed will be filed after funds clear.

sections.h2: Questions to put to a buyer
sections.html:
Put the same questions to every buyer and keep the answers in writing. That makes two offers easy to compare, even when one looks larger.

  • Is the price firm, and what could change it after an inspection?
  • Does the buyer need a loan, or is it a cash purchase with proof of funds?
  • Who pays for the title search, the attorney and the recording?
  • How many days will the buyer take to close?
  • Will the buyer take the house with the furniture and debris still in it?

Cash Home Buyers gives written answers on Gastonia houses, including inherited homes, rentals and vacant properties.

Cash does not remove the legal steps. You still prove title, pay off loans and liens, and sign a deed that your attorney records. What it removes is the buyer's mortgage approval and appraisal, the round of repair requests after an inspection, and the weeks of showings.

For a Gastonia house with an old roof, tired wiring or a tenant who will not leave, those skipped steps are where the time goes in a listing. Ask a cash buyer to put the price, closing date and who pays each fee in writing, then compare the amount you would keep against a listing's net after repairs, commission and carrying costs.

sections.h2: A step-by-step plan for the weeks ahead
sections.html:
Start by confirming who owns the house on paper. Next, get a payoff letter from each lender and ask the tax office whether anything is owed. Then walk the house with an inspector or contractor so you know the repair total before any buyer names a price.

Once offers arrive, ask each buyer for a written closing date and a list of which fees land on you. Pick the offer that leaves the most money in your hands with the fewest unknowns, not the biggest headline number. Your attorney then searches title, prepares the deed and files it once funds clear.

If anyone lives in the house, tell each buyer at the first call. Keep notices, the lease and any court papers together so an attorney can read them quickly.

faqs.q: Is Gastonia the Gaston County seat?
How often does Gaston County reappraise?
faqs.a: Every four years, a cycle the commissioners adopted in 2025.

faqs.q: Where is a Gastonia deed filed?
faqs.a: With the Gaston County register of deeds, usually by the closing attorney.

faqs.q: I inherited a house in Gastonia. Can I sell it?
faqs.a: Yes, once you hold legal authority to sign. G.S. 28A-25-1 describes a small estate affidavit, and the court clerk can say which route fits.
